A series of alternate development patterns were considered and projections made for each one. The following discussion focuses on the projections developed under the situation considered most likely to occur, that is, the converging Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR-2) with a projected significant peripheral Crow coal development (AF-2). It should be mentioned that due to uncertainties currently associated with the leases held by various companies and the resultant postponement of development plans, the figures projected for AF-1 (no nearby coal development), are probably a more accurate view of what will occur in the immediate future (until 1980). This fact should be kept in mind when assessing projected impacts discussed in this statement.
Population and Households - Prior to examining the pattern of total population growth, 1/1 it is helpful to note the growth patterns of the Crow and non-Crow components of the population. The Crows have a comparatively high rate of natural increase which, if continued, will result in a steady population increase from 4,002 in 1975 to 9,120 by 2000. This represents a population increase of 128 percent. Historically, the vast majority of Crows have resided on the Reservation.
